lines.trans: Our son is staying at grandma's tonight.
Everything is fine, we will be going soon.
It seems she is very rowdy tonight.
In this state she might jump out of the car.
Katya, will you help me get Nastya home?
Of course, let us go get in the car quickly.
Sorry, brother, you see for yourself what the situation is.
I want to ask about the hospital.
Tell me, is everything really alright with you?
Of course, everything is completely normal with me.
All of our waiters have suddenly disappeared somewhere.
Apparently I will have to serve the dish myself.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Любимый мужчина готовит мне вкусный ужин.
examples.trans: My beloved man is cooking me a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Смотри, твой су-шеф сейчас звонит.
examples.trans: Look, your sous-chef is calling right now.

examples.text: Поставь телефон на громкую связь.
examples.trans: Put the phone on speakerphone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'овершенно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Оказывается, ты у меня совершенно здоров!
examples.trans: It turns out you are completely healthy!

examples.text: Конечно, со мной всё совершенно нормально.
examples.trans: Of course, everything is completely normal with me.

examples.text: Совершенно верно, я мэр этого города.
examples.trans: Quite right, I am the mayor of this town.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, со мной всё совершенно нормально.
examples.trans: Of course, everything is completely normal with me.

examples.text: Да всё нормально будет, дорогая Настя.
examples.trans: Everything will be just fine, dear Nastya.

examples.text: Всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Куда-то все наши официанты вдруг пропали.
examples.trans: All of our waiters have suddenly disappeared somewhere.

examples.text: Мэр куда-то спрятал деньги.
examples.trans: The mayor has hidden the money somewhere.

examples.text: Он куда-то ушёл.
examples.trans: He's gone off somewhere.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: С тобой сегодня вечером так весело!
examples.trans: It is so much fun with you tonight!

examples.text: С ним за столом всегда так весело!
examples.trans: It is always so cheerful at the table with him!

examples.text: Всё нормально.
examples.trans: Everything's fine.

meanings.note: From German 'Offiziant' / Late Latin 'officians' (one who performs a duty or service).

examples.text: Куда-то все наши официанты вдруг пропали.
examples.trans: All of our waiters have suddenly disappeared somewhere.

examples.text: Официант вежливо приветствует новых гостей.
examples.trans: The waiter politely greets the new guests.

examples.text: Пожалуйста, не загораживайте проход официантам.
examples.trans: Please do not block the walkway for the waiters.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'suddenly, what if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: С чего ты это вдруг взяла?
examples.trans: What made you think that all of a sudden?

examples.text: Куда-то все наши официанты вдруг пропали.
examples.trans: All of our waiters have suddenly disappeared somewhere.

examples.text: Вот откуда, значит, это новоселье вдруг взялось!
examples.trans: So that is where this housewarming suddenly came from!

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'пасть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to disappear, vanish'.

examples.text: Самсонов пропал.
examples.trans: Samsonov is missing.

examples.text: Аркадий, что делать будем? Самсонов пропал.
examples.trans: Arkady, what are we going to do? Samsonov is missing.

examples.text: Таня, а куда пропал твой бывший муж?
examples.trans: Tanya, and where did your former husband disappear to?

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Извини, брат, сам видишь, какая ситуация.
examples.trans: Sorry, brother, you see for yourself what the situation is.

examples.text: Видимо, придётся мне самому блюдо подать.
examples.trans: Apparently I will have to serve the dish myself.

examples.text: Но, видимо, я зря зашёл.
examples.trans: But apparently I came in vain.

meanings.en: to have to, to be forced to
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'йтись'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'it will be necessary', paired with 'приходиться'.

examples.text: Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: I'm going to have to torture you.

examples.text: Нам пришлось долго ждать.
examples.trans: We had to wait a long time.

examples.text: Ты что, очкарик, не понимаешь? Мне тебя мучить придётся.
examples.trans: Don't you get it, four-eyes? I'm going to have to torture you.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'dish' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Видимо, придётся мне самому блюдо подать.
examples.trans: Apparently I will have to serve the dish myself.

examples.text: Тем более фирменное блюдо у тебя уже есть.
examples.trans: Especially since you already have a signature dish.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'дать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to submit, file; to serve', paired with 'подавать'.

examples.text: Угощайся, это подарок за счёт заведения.
examples.trans: Enjoy, it is a gift on the house.

examples.text: Видимо, придётся мне самому блюдо подать.
examples.trans: Apparently I will have to serve the dish myself.

examples.text: Ты подарила ему свой прощальный поцелуй?
examples.trans: Did you give him your farewell kiss?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'forgive', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.text: Прости, пожалуйста, мне пора идти работать.
examples.trans: Excuse me, please, it is time for me to go work.

examples.text: Прости, мне нужно нести заказ.
examples.trans: Forgive me, I need to carry the order.

examples.text: Простите нас, пожалуйста, за этот обман.
examples.trans: Forgive us, please, for this deception.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Кате точно нужно надёжное мужское плечо.
examples.trans: Katya definitely needs a reliable man's shoulder.

examples.text: Прости, мне нужно нести заказ.
examples.trans: Forgive me, I need to carry the order.

examples.text: Мне через час нужно срочно отъехать.
examples.trans: I need to leave urgently in an hour.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bring, carry', paired with 'понести'.

examples.text: Прости, мне нужно нести заказ.
examples.trans: Forgive me, I need to carry the order.

examples.text: Юля, неси ручку.
examples.trans: Yulia, bring a pen.

examples.text: Я несу вещи.
examples.trans: I'm carrying the things.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты уже закончил работу, Лёва?
examples.trans: Have you finished work already, Lyova?

examples.text: Ладно, давай закажем себе по коктейлю.
examples.trans: Alright, let us order ourselves a cocktail each.

examples.text: А у вас тут закрытая вечеринка?
examples.trans: Are you having a private party here?
